Q: Render HTML elements simultaneously A:
  • Give them visibility: hidden (or similar) initially and overwrite that using a tag that comes after them in the HTML code:
    • a <script> tag
    • or a <style> tag
    • or for example <span class="young-sibling"> that will trigger :has(+ .young-sibling) { visibility: visible; }
  • or create those elements programmatically in a single <script> instead of including them in the HTML code.

For elements such as <img> and <iframe>, you may additionally want to wait for the load event of each of them. For example, if you want to show such an element simultaneously with one that doesn't have a load event, you have to choose the option above of overwriting visiblity with <scipt> and wait both for that <scipt> to get reached as well as the load event to occur before making them visible.

Q: Android/PyQt6: Error while fetching response from Gemini API using google-genai SDK A:

Looking closely at your code snippet and your use of the new google-genai SDK, there is a very high probability that the error is caused by a slight syntax mismatch in how you are passing the configuration.

In the new google-genai SDK, configuration parameters like system_instruction and temperature are passed inside a dictionary (or a configuration object) using the config parameter, but the syntax depends on whether you are using a dictionary or the strict GenerateContentConfig class.

The Fix: Correcting the config Syntax

If you are using types.GenerateContentConfig, you need to make sure the arguments match the SDK's expected properties. Alternatively, the google-genai SDK natively accepts a standard Python dictionary for the config parameter, which is often much easier to manage.

Try updating your API call to use a dictionary for the configuration:

from google import genai

client = genai.Client()

# Pass the configuration as a standard dictionary
response = client.models.generate_content(
    model='gemini-2.5-pro',
    contents=user_content,
    config={
        'system_instruction': system_instruction,
        'temperature': 0.3,
        'response_mime_type': 'application/json'
    },
)

raw_text = response.text.strip()

Pro-Tip for JSON Generation

Since you are asking Gemini to return JSON for a specific structure (generated_files), relying only on response_mime_type="application/json" can sometimes result in arbitrary JSON keys.

To make your code incredibly robust against parsing errors, you can provide a Structured Schema using Pydantic. This forces Gemini to return the exact JSON structure your PyQt6 application expects.

from google import genai
from pydantic import BaseModel

# 1. Define the structure you expect back
class GeneratedFile(BaseModel):
    filename: str
    content: str

class WebpackResponse(BaseModel):
    files: list[GeneratedFile]

client = genai.Client()

# 2. Pass the schema in the config
response = client.models.generate_content(
    model='gemini-2.5-pro',
    contents=user_content,
    config={
        'system_instruction': system_instruction,
        'temperature': 0.3,
        'response_mime_type': 'application/json',
        'response_schema': WebpackResponse, # Enforces the exact structure
    },
)

# 3. The SDK automatically parses it into your Pydantic model!
# No need for json.loads(response.text)
result = response.parsed
for file in result.files:
    print(f"Writing {file.filename}...")
    # write file.content to disk

Still seeing an error?

If updating the config structure doesn't solve it, could you paste the exact error message you are seeing in your console? (Also, double-check if the error is a google.genai.errors.APIError or a PyQt6 QThread cross-threading issue!)

Q: How can I use system CA certificates (Debian/Ubuntu) with Python's Requests? A:

Requests uses Certifi as the default root certificates package, which builds in a lot of good CAs, but it is unable to modify them.

Debian (and Ubuntu) maintainers changed Certifi's behavior different from the default:

def where():
    return "/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt"

So if you use the APT-installed packages requests and certifi, there isn’t any problem.

But pip3 installed Certifi inside a virtual environment uses builtin CAs. So it is unable to use the update-ca-certificates mechanism. Besides manually specifying the root certificate in the application code (which may not be possible if request is called indirectly through third-party interfaces), it can also overriding with enviroument variable REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE=/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt to emulate the Debianized behavor.

Q: Android x86 9.0 Ethernet Connection on Physical Machine A:

Se soluciona, agregando en GRUB lo siguiente:

    EXTMOD=realtek VIRT_WIFI=0

Por ejemplo: En una maquina (dos sistemas operativos en una misma PC) con: Debian y Android, actualizar el Grub, desde Debian, asi:

  1. Observar cuales son las condiciones iniciales, por ejemplo:

     hd0 es el disco duro: /dev/sda
 msdos2 es la particion 2: /dev/sda2
 android-9.0-r2 es la carpeta que crea el instalador de Android: /dev/sda2/android-9.0-r2

  2. Añadir lo siguiente a /etc/grub.d/40_custom:

     menuentry 'My Android-x86' --class android-x86 {
 savedefault
 set root='hd0,msdos2'
 linux /android-9.0-r2/kernel quiet EXTMOD=realtek VIRT_WIFI=0 root=/dev/ram0 SRC=/android-9.0-r2
 initrd /android-9.0-r2/initrd.img
 }

  3. Ejecutar, tambien desde Debian:

     sudo update-grub
 sudo grub-install /dev/sda

  4. Verificar desde Android, use:

     ALT + F1 (Ir modo texto)
 cat /proc/cmdline
 ifconfig -a
 ALT + F7 (Retornar al modo GUI)

  5. Revisar fuentes:

https://groups.google.com/g/android-x86/c/HznhzwaMAXk

http://git.osdn.net/view?p=android-x86/device-generic-common.git;a=patch;h=8ac9fea0db77ce1ace33e04a0da9def54a92ac55

Q: The specified object was not found in the store., The process failed to get the correct properties A:

That error is happening because the user I try to impersonate is a new user and never log in to OWA even once... when I logged into OWA it worked...

It sounds like the Mailbox hasn't been provisioned and logging into OWA is just kicking off that process. Using EWS alone won't do the provisioning the easiest way it just send an Email to the Mailbox. Another method I've used in the past is if you run Test-MapiConnectivity https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/exchange/mailboxes/test-mapiconnectivity?view=exchange-ps from the Exchange Management Shell before you run your EWS code that will always ensure that the Mailbox has been provisioned.
